newsitem.title: USA: IMF approves $45 mln, three-year loan to Mongolia.
newsitem.headline: IMF approves $45 mln, three-year loan to Mongolia.

text.p: The International Monetary Fund has approved a $45 million loan to Mongolia and expects the economy there to grow by up to six percent a year between now and the year 2000, an IMF statement said on Thursday.

The fund said the three-year Enhanced Structural Adjustment Facility was designed to support market-oriented reforms in Mongolia. Mongolia would receive $15 million in the first year, divided into two semi-annual installments.

"The program's medium-term objectives are to reduce inflation to single-digit rates, achieve an annual real growth rate of six percent and increase official gross international reserves to the equivalent of six weeks cover," the IMF said.

"The budget deficit will be reduced to six percent of GDP in 2000 from 10.5 percent in 1997. The fiscal adjustment will be achieved by reducing the size of the public sector and reforms in public administration and taxation."
The IMF projected GDP growth of three percent in 1997, rising to five percent in 1998 and six percent in 1999 and 2000. GDP growth was 2.6 percent in 1996.
Inflation is seen falling to 31 percent this year, from 58.8 percent in 1996. Inflation of 13 percent is expected in 1998, 6.2 percent in 1999 and 6.0 percent in 2000.
